content: The following references provide detailed insights into various aspects of public health, non-communicable diseases (NCDs), and public-private partnerships (PPPs) in healthcare: 1. A guide for managing conflicts of interest in public pharmaceutical-sector committees in lowand middle-income countries was accessed on August 4, 2023. 2. Policy considerations for public-private partnerships in healthcare infrastructure and services in middle-income European countries were reviewed on May 12, 2023. 3. Decision WHA74(11) highlights the role of the global coordination mechanism in preventing and controlling NCDs through multistakeholder engagement, as discussed during the 74th World Health Assembly (May 24–June 1, 2021). 4. The WHO Independent High-Level Commission on NCDs released its final report, emphasizing the need for actionable steps, titled It's Time to Walk the Talk, accessed on May 12, 2023. 5. The third edition of Making Health Policy by Buse et al. (2023) provides a comprehensive framework for health policy development. 6. Hawkes and Buse (2011) critically examine the interaction between the public health sector and the food industry, calling for clarity in defining partnerships and transparency in underlying interests. 7. The United Nations Environment Programme (2019) outlined a strategy for private sector engagement, emphasizing sustainable development goals. 8. The Global Fund's framework on private sector engagement was reviewed on May 12, 2023. 9. WHO's technical packages, such as SHAKE for salt reduction and SAFER for alcohol harm reduction, provide actionable strategies for addressing NCD risk factors. 10. The WHO's plan to eliminate industrially produced trans-fatty acids from the global food supply was announced on May 14, 2018. 11. The HEARTS technical package offers guidance on cardiovascular disease management in primary healthcare settings. 12. 13. The WHO Procurement Report (2020) provides insights into global health procurement practices. 14. The Guidelines for Implementation of Article 13 on Tobacco Advertising, Promotion, and Sponsorship emphasize the importance of regulating tobacco marketing to protect public health. 15. The WHO's guidelines on protecting children from harmful food marketing impacts were reviewed on January 10, 2024. 16. The Codex Alimentarius serves as a global standard for food safety and quality. 17. A global review of quality and accreditation in healthcare services highlights best practices and challenges in achieving universal health coverage. 18. The WHO's Evidence, Policy, Impact guide supports evidence-informed decision-making in public health. 19. The Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (2011) outline the responsibilities of businesses in upholding human rights. 20. The WHO's Package of Essential Non-Communicable Disease Interventions (PEN) provides a framework for integrating NCD prevention and management into primary healthcare. 21. 22. The SDG Partnership Guidebook offers practical guidance for building impactful multistakeholder partnerships to achieve sustainable development goals. 23. The WHO's Time to Deliver report (2018) underscores the urgency of addressing NCDs through coordinated global efforts. 24. A systematic review by De Pinho Campos et al. (2011) evaluates public-private partnerships in product development for public health. 25. Wakefield et al. (2020) discuss the effectiveness of mass media campaigns in influencing health behavior change. 26. The OECD's Peer Inventory 1 provides terminology and typology for private sector engagement in health. 27. The WHO's Legal Environment Assessment for the Prevention of NCDs serves as an operational guide for policymakers. 28. The Risk Assessment Tool (2015) by the United Nations Development Programme aids in evaluating responsible business conduct. 29. The WHO's Handbook for Non-State Actors outlines engagement strategies with the organization. 30. The Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises emphasize ethical business practices and corporate responsibility. 31. 32. The Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact provide a framework for sustainable and socially responsible business practices. 33. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Surveillance and Monitoring initiatives, such as the STEPS approach, offer tools for tracking NCD risk factors. 34. The Global Adult Tobacco Survey provides data on tobacco use patterns and informs tobacco control policies. 35. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Prevention and Control: A Guidance Note for Investment Cases supports resource allocation for NCD interventions. 36. The Country Connector on Private Sector in Health serves as a repository of tools for engaging private sector entities in healthcare. 37. A systematic review by Roehrich et al. (2014) evaluates the health impact of public-private partnerships. 38. The WHO's Strategy for Private Sector Engagement 2021–2025 outlines approaches for leveraging private sector contributions to public health. 39. The Guidelines for Public-Private Engagement by the World Meteorological Organization (2021) provide a framework for collaboration. 40. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Surveillance, Monitoring, and Reporting initiatives emphasize the importance of data-driven decision-making. 41. The Evaluation of Pharmaceutical Industry-Led Access Programs by Rockers et al. (2019) proposes a standardized framework for assessing such initiatives. 42. 43. The Private Sector Contributions Towards Universal Health Coverage statement highlights the role of private entities in achieving health equity. 44. The WHO's Guidelines for Public-Private Engagement in Nutrition address governance challenges in tackling malnutrition. 45. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Prevention and Control: A Guidance Note for Investment Cases supports strategic planning for NCD interventions. 46. The WHO's Guidelines for Public-Private Engagement in Nutrition address governance challenges in tackling malnutrition. 47. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Prevention and Control: A Guidance Note for Investment Cases supports strategic planning for NCD interventions. 48. The WHO's Guidelines for Public-Private Engagement in Nutrition address governance challenges in tackling malnutrition. 49. The WHO's Non-Communicable Disease Prevention and Control: A Guidance Note for Investment Cases supports strategic planning for NCD interventions. 50. The WHO's Guidelines for Public-Private Engagement in Nutrition address governance challenges in tackling malnutrition. These references collectively provide a wealth of information on global health policies, strategies for NCD prevention, and the role of public-private partnerships in advancing healthcare objectives.
